content:
sai: noticing a bunch of gRPC streaming stalls for long-lived inference connections between pods. errors show 'stream reset by peer' + lots of retransmits. started around 02:15 UTC when we rolled a new model version.

nate: which nodes/azs are affected?

sai: cross-node, us-west1-b -> us-west1-c, mostly nodepool-gpu. tcpdump shows fragmented IPs on the path :eyes:

marta: is this RDMA or standard TCP over overlay?

sai: it's TCP over VXLAN overlay. RDMA traffic looks funky too on the same nodepair (timeouts for CUDA heartbeat).

luis: ran a quick check on two nodes: `ip link show dev eth0` returned mtu 1500 on node A and mtu 8982 on node B (one had jumbo frames). ethtool -k shows GRO/GSO enabled for vxlan.

sai: snippet from pcap:```
# tcpdump -n -r dump.pcap | grep Fragmented
IP (frag 0) 10.0.2.4 > 10.0.3.9: Flags [none], proto TCP, 0:1448(1448) ...
IP (frag 1) 10.0.2.4 > 10.0.3.9: Flags [none], proto TCP, 1448:2896(1448) ...
```

marta: giant packets on one end + standard MTU on other = fragmentation after encapsulation. gRPC/HTTP2 streaming is sensitive because frames get split across fragments and kernel reassembly delays cause stream windows to stall.

nate: what's the customer visible hit?

sai: GPU clusters saw tail latency spikes (x10) and the autoscaler spun up extra nodes; queued inference tasks increased and cost bumped ~18% in the incident window.

luis: short-term mitigation that worked on a test node: clamp MTU on egress to avoid fragmentation. two options: set VXLAN mtu lower in CNI or use iptables TCPMSS clamp on host. example I used: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360` — retransmits dropped and streams stabilized.

marta: can we canary that? apply clamp to 5% of nodepool and monitor. also consider setting vxlan mtu=1450 to be safe.

nate: another safety net: disable LRO/GSO on host NIC for overlay to avoid kernel offload reassembly oddities: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` — helped in my local repro.

infra-bot: deploy job started: canary=gpupool-2 nodes=3

sai: we should add PMTU and fragmentation alerts. suggestion: alert when pcap shows 'IP (frag' + grpc-reset-rate > 1/min.

luis: opening a provider ticket to check whether their fabric applied any MTU clamp on the path. looks like a PMTU negotiation mismatch between host and underlay.

marta: follow-ups: 1) canary rollout status in 1h 2) add per-route MTU label in Console + surface in route diagnostics 3) run an RDMA fallback verification job for the gpu nodepool.

nate: created incident INF-4271 and added cost impact notes.

sai: thanks all — will post updates from the canary. :thumbsup:
